column3: “To your mouth a horn” is rendered “Put the trumpet to your lips!”; NASB supplies “the enemy comes.”
“We know you, Israel” is rendered “we of Israel know You.”
“Made kings” is rendered “set up kings”; NASB adds “it.”
“He has rejected” follows the Hebrew; NASB adds “saying” before “My anger burns,” and renders “not be able innocence” as “be incapable of innocence.”
“For from Israel and it” is rendered “For from Israel is even this!”; “fragments” is rendered “broken to pieces.”
“Growth” is rendered “heads”; NASB keeps the wordplay in sense only, with “Should it yield.”
NASB supplies “allies” and renders “a few from the burden” as “diminish because of the burden”; “a king, princes” is rendered “the king of princes.”
“For sinning” is rendered “for sin” and “of sinning.”
“The numerous things” is rendered “ten thousand precepts”; NASB adds “Though.”
“The sacrifices of my gifts” is rendered “My sacrificial gifts”; “punish sins” is rendered “punish them for their sins.”
